subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should high-priority system events bypass the active session lane as prompt-visible transcript content, or should urgent alerts use a separate operator-visible TUI/Gateway notification surface with ordered transcript injection later?
rationale: The current request crosses a trust boundary because system events become `System:` prompt content, and only maintainers can choose the ordering, spoofing, and operator-visibility contract.

options.title: Separate urgent alert from transcript injection
options.body: Add an immediate operator-visible alert path and keep prompt/transcript mutation ordered through the existing system-event queue or a reviewed ordered variant.

options.title: Add a prompt-visible bypass contract
options.body: Permit trusted callers to inject directly into prompt-visible session state, but require explicit authorization, ordering, sanitization, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep existing best-effort semantics
options.body: Document that `--mode now` is wake-only and rely on out-of-band channels such as Telegram for real-time outage alerts.

recommendation.title: Separate urgent alert from transcript injection
recommendation.body: Add an immediate operator-visible alert path and keep prompt/transcript mutation ordered through the existing system-event queue or a reviewed ordered variant.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway and prompt-boundary history makes this the best available owner for the product/security boundary choice.
